name: CarKey
summary: Access the remote keyless features of configured vehicles in the Wallet app.

declarations.name: ActionIdentifier
declarations.comment:
A type that stores the designation code for one of
the actions that a vehicle feature supports.

An ``ActionIdentifier`` type wraps a vehicle-specific code you
define. This code — known as the action identifier — corresponds
to an action your vehicle can take for a particular feature.
For example, you might define actions to lock or unlock the
vehicle’s doors. Use this type in conjunction with a specific
``FunctionIdentifier`` type to specify the complete action you
want to perform on a vehicle.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Creates and returns a new action identifier with the specified value.

- Parameters:
    - rawValue: The value for the new type.
- Returns: A new action identifier type.

members.name: rawValue
members.comment: The raw value that corresponds to the feature-specific action.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Creates and returns a new action identifier with the specified value.

- Parameters:
    - rawValue: The value for the new type.
- Returns: A new action identifier type.

declarations.name: ActionIdentifier.RawValue
declarations.comment:
The raw type that can be used to represent all values of the conforming
type.

Every distinct value of the conforming type has a corresponding unique
value of the `RawValue` type, but there may be values of the `RawValue`
type that don't have a corresponding value of the conforming type.

declarations.name: CarKeyErrorCode
declarations.comment: The errors that can occur when you perform remote-keyless entry operations on a vehicle.

declarations.name: CarKeyRemoteControl
declarations.comment:
The object you use to start a new vehicle-related session.

Use a ``CarKeyRemoteControl`` object to create the session
your app uses to communicate with the vehicles your company
manufactures. You don’t create an instance of this object.
Instead, call the ``start(delegate:subscriptionRange:with:)``
class method to request a new session object. The system
retrieves the relevant vehicle information from person's Apple
Wallet and adds vehicles that match your company's make to
the session.

Start a new session only when your app is running in the foreground.
If your app enters the background, end the current session and
start a new one when your app returns to the foreground.

members.name: registerForLaunchOnCarKeyEvent
members.comment:
Register your app to be relaunched in the background on CarKey events.
Under certain conditions the system will not relaunch the app regardless of CarKey events.

Because of user actions, it’s possible that an app may no longer be eligible to be relaunched in response to CarKey events.
Therefore it’s important to educate the users of your app, so that they understand how their actions impact its functionality.

Well designed apps will be resilient under such conditions.

Registered apps will be relaunched on CarKey events under the following conditions:
- App removed from memory (while having an active CarKeyRemoteControlSession)
- App crashed (while having an active CarKeyRemoteControlSession)
- Device restarted and unlocked for the first time

members.name: unregisterForLaunchOnCarKeyEvent
members.comment: Unregister your app so it's no longer relaunched in the background on CarKey events.

members.name: start
members.signature: class func start(delegate: any CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate, subscriptionRange subscriptionFunctionIDRange: ClosedRange<Int>? = nil, with delegateCallbackQueue: DispatchQueue? = nil) async throws -> CarKeyRemoteControlSession
members.comment:
Creates and returns a new session object to access the
provisioned vehicles.

This method creates a new session object each time you call it.
You can have only one active session at a time. If you call
this method while a session is already active, the method waits
until the previous session becomes invalid before returning the
new session. The session object gives you access to the vehicles that
your company makes and that the owner added to their Apple Wallet.

- Parameters:
  - delegate: The object you use to receive data from the
  vehicle and handle connection issues. You must specify this
  object at session-creation time, and can only change it by
  creating a new session. This object must adopt the
  ``CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate`` protocol.
  - subscriptionFunctionIDRange: The range of function IDs your
  app supports for the current session. Each vehicle feature you
  can control remotely has an associated function identifier code.
  Use this parameter to limit the features accessible to the current
  person. For example, you might include a subset of features to
  limit the actions of someone who isn't the vehicle's primary owner.
  - delegateCallbackQueue: The queue on which to execute the methods
  of your delegate object. If you specify `nil`, CarKey creates a new
  serial dispatch queue for you.
- Returns: A new session object.
members.typescript: static start(delegate: Implements<CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate> | SDKHandle, subscriptionFunctionIDRange?: (SDKHandle) | null, delegateCallbackQueue?: (_Dispatch_DispatchQueue) | null): Promise<CarKeyRemoteControlSession>

declarations.name: CarKeyRemoteControlSession
declarations.comment:
The object that manages communication with the vehicles
you manufacture.

A `CarKeyRemoteControlSession` object coordinates interactions
between your app and your company's make of vehicles.
This object works with the system to transmit data securely to
and from a vehicle, and to report results back to your app. Use
this object to send commands or data directly to a vehicle, and
to get information about the available vehicles and their current
configuration.

Don’t create this object directly. Instead, call the
``CarKeyRemoteControl/start(delegate:subscriptionRange:with:)``
method to create a new session object. When you finish interacting with
the vehicle, call the session’s ``CarKeyRemoteControlSession/end()``
method to close out the session and prevent further access. You can have
only one active session at a time. If you try to start a second
session, ``CarKeyRemoteControl/start(delegate:subscriptionRange:with:)``
doesn't return until the currently active session becomes invalid.

When you configure a new session, provide a delegate object to receive
data from vehicle-initiated transfers. The system also uses your delegate
notify you when the configuration of a vehicle changes. For example,
it lets you know when connectivity to the vehicle changes. The delegate
must adopt the ``CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate`` protocol.

- Note: If your app has an active session, the system automatically
ends that session when your app enters the background. Upon reentering
the foreground, you must create a new session to communicate with your
vehicle again.

members.name: vehicleReports
members.comment:
The configuration details of the provisioned vehicles that
match your company’s make.

The system maintains a cache of provisioned vehicles and updates
that information when the configuration details change.

members.name: sendPassthroughData
members.signature: func sendPassthroughData(_ passthroughData: Data, toVehicle vehicleID: String) throws
members.comment:
Sends the specified custom data to the vehicle.

Use this method to send data that is custom to your specific vehicle.
This method passes the data unmodified directly to the vehicle, and
it is up to you to format the data exactly how the vehicle needs it.

If the vehicle sends a custom response, the system delivers it to
the ``CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate/remoteControlSession(_:didReceivePassthroughData:fromVehicle:)``
method of your session’s delegate object.

- Parameters:
  - passthroughData: The custom data to send to the vehicle. Make
  sure the size of your data object doesn’t exceed 65 kilobytes.
  - vehicleID: The target vehicle for the request. Choose the vehicle
from one of the session’s vehicle reports. Specify the string in the
``VehicleReport/identifier`` property of the corresponding report.

members.name: isPassiveEntryAvailable
members.signature: func isPassiveEntryAvailable(forVehicle vehicleID: String) throws -> Bool
members.comment:
Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether passive entry is
currently available for the specified vehicle.

- Parameter vehicleID: The target vehicle for the request. Choose the
  vehicle from one of the session’s vehicle reports. Specify
  the string in the ``VehicleReport/identifier`` property of the corresponding
  report.
- Returns: `true` if passive entry is available, or `false` if the
feature is not available.

members.name: end
members.comment:
Ends the session and stops the delivery of notifications
for all vehicles in the session.

When you no longer need to access the vehicle information,
call this method to end the session. If the session isn’t
currently active when you call this method, it throws an error.

The system automatically ends a session when your app enters
the background. Upon reentering the foreground, you must create
a new session to communicate with your vehicle again.

members.name: sign
members.signature: func sign(data: Data, forVehicle vehicleID: String) throws -> CarKeyRemoteControlSession.Attestation
members.comment:
Sign data with the endpoint.SK identified by vehicleIdentifier
as described in the section "OEM App Data Attestation" of
the Car Connectivity Consortium Digital Key Release 3.0 specification.

This method can only be used while the application is in the foreground.

- Parameter data: The OEM App Data to sign.
- Parameter vehicleID: The vehicle identifier.
- Returns: An Attestation object.

members.name: perform
members.comment:
Sends a request to the vehicle to start an action that has a
separate stopping point, and optionally allows your app to
have control over incoming continuation requests and to
exchange data during the execution of the action.

Call this method for vehicle features that that have both a start
and stop point. For example, use it to start raising or lowering
the top of a convertible. This method sends the request to the
vehicle asynchronously.

Use the returned object to get the execution status of the initial
request, and to optionally stop the action.

- Parameter action: The action to perform. Use this object to specify the
  action to perform and the vehicle on which to perform it.
- Parameter continuationStrategy: The continuation strategy.
- Returns: An object you use to get the results of the initial
request and stop the action.

members.name: perform
members.signature: func perform(_ action: RemoteKeylessEntryAction) throws -> RemoteKeylessEntryAction.ExecutionRequest
members.comment:
Sends a request to the vehicle to perform a one-time action.

Call this method when the vehicle feature involves a one-time action.
For example, use it to lock the doors of the vehicle. This method sends
the request to the vehicle asynchronously.

Use the returned object to get the execution status of the specified
request. The execution status indicates whether the vehicle completed
the action successfully or an error occurred.

- Parameter action: The one-time action to perform. Use this object to
  specify the action you want to perform and the vehicle on which
  to perform it.
- Returns: An object you use to get the results of the request.

members.comment:

Use the returned object to get the execution status of the initial

- Returns: An object you use to get the results of the initial

declarations.name: CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate
declarations.comment:
An interface you use to receive session- and vehicle-related
information from the system.

The system uses the ``CarKeyRemoteControlSessionDelegate`` protocol to
notify your app asynchronously when something happens. Adopt this
protocol in one of your objects and detect when the system invalidates
the session. If your vehicle is capable of sending data to your app, you
also use this protocol to receive any data the vehicle sends.

declarations.name: RemoteKeylessEntryAction
declarations.comment:
An automatically ending action that you want to perform on
a vehicle.

Use a ``RemoteKeylessEntryAction`` object to store details about
an action that runs to completion after you start it. For example,
you might use this type of action to unlock the door locks of
the vehicle. The object stores information about the feature
you want to control and the action to take on that feature.
It also stores the identifier for the vehicle itself.

After you create a ``RemoteKeylessEntryAction`` object, call your
session's ``CarKeyRemoteControlSession/perform(_:)-8ac0c`` method
to execute the action. Use the returned
``RemoteKeylessEntryAction/ExecutionRequest``
object to determine the success or failure of the request.

members.name: init
members.signature: init(functionID: FunctionIdentifier, actionID: ActionIdentifier, vehicleID: String)
members.comment:
Creates a new action object with the specified action-specific
details and vehicle ID.

This method creates an immutable action object that you can
pass to your session’s ``CarKeyRemoteControlSession/perform(_:)-8ac0c``
method.

- Parameters:
  - functionID: The vehicle-specific code that identifies the
  feature to activate. For example, the vehicle might have a
  specific code to access the door locks.
  - actionID: The vehicle-specific code that defines what action
  to take on the vehicle feature. For example, a vehicle might have
  separate actions to lock and unlock the vehicle’s doors.
  - vehicleID: The target vehicle for the action. Choose the vehicle
  from one of the session’s vehicle reports. Specify the string
  in the ``VehicleReport/identifier`` property of the corresponding report.
- Returns: An action object with the specified information.
members.typescript: static init(functionID: FunctionIdentifier, actionID: ActionIdentifier, vehicleID: string): RemoteKeylessEntryAction

members.name: functionID
members.comment:
The vehicle-specific code that identifies which feature you
want to control.

You define the function identifiers for your vehicles
and what features they represent.

members.name: recipientVehicleID
members.comment:
The vehicle to receive the action request.

This string is the same one that appears in the ``VehicleReport/identifier``
property of one of the session's vehicle reports.

members.name: actionID
members.comment:
The vehicle-specific code that identifies what action
to take on the targeted feature.

You define the action identifiers for your vehicles and
what actions they perform on the vehicle function.

declarations.name: RemoteKeylessEntryAction.ExecutionRequest
declarations.comment:
An object that reports the results of an automatically ending
action asynchronously.

When you perform an action, the system creates a
``RemoteKeylessEntryAction/ExecutionRequest`` object for that
request and returns it to your app. Use that object to asynchronously
determine whether your request completed successfully or reported
an error.

members.name: results
members.signature: final func results() async throws -> ExecutionStatus
members.comment:
Returns the results of a preceding action request.

After you call your session’s ``CarKeyRemoteControlSession/perform(_:)-8ac0c``
method to send an action request to a vehicle, call this method
and await the results of that request. Upon the successful completion
of the request, this method returns the vehicle-provided status code.
If an error occurs, this method throws the error instead.

- Returns: A structure that contains the vehicle-specific status
code from the vehicle.

After you create a ``RemoteKeylessEntryConfigurableEnduringAction`` object, call

declarations.name: VehicleReport
declarations.comment:
A type that contains information about a vehicle configured for
remote keyless entry in the user’s Apple Wallet.

A `VehicleReport` type provides information about a vehicle
you manufacture. The system generates a vehicle report for each
vehicle that matches your company's make, and that the owner
configured in their Apple Wallet. Use a vehicle report to get
information about the vehicle, such as whether it's currently
connected and able to receive commands. You can also use the
report to determine which vehicle features you can operate
from your app.

A vehicle can optionally attach proprietary data to one of its function
identifiers. You might use this data to support additional features
related to that vehicle feature. For example, you might want to
attach a unique security code to the door lock function. Use the vehicle
report to retrieve any data your vehicle sends. If the vehicle
sends new data, the system updates the report and notifies your
session delegate.

members.name: identifier
members.comment:
The string you use to identify the vehicle when making requests.

Use this string to differentiate vehicles associated with the
session, and to ensure you send requests to the correct vehicle.

members.name: isConnected
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the vehicle is currently
connected over Bluetooth.

The value of this property is `true` when the vehicle is connected
over Bluetooth, or `false` when it isn’t connected.

members.name: proprietaryData
members.signature: func proprietaryData(for function: FunctionIdentifier) throws -> Data?
members.comment:
Retrieves the proprietary data associated with one of the
vehicle’s functions.

When it receives new data from a vehicle, the system updates
the vehicle report and notifies the session delegate. Call
this method to retrieve any data associated with a particular
feature of your vehicle.
- Parameter function: The function identifier for the given vehicle
  feature. If you specify an unknown feature, this method throws
  an error. For a list of the vehicle’s supported features,
  see the ``supportedFunctions`` property.
- Returns: A data object, or `nil` if no data was present for
the specified feature.

members.name: supportedFunctions
members.comment:
An array of function identifiers that indicates the features
the vehicle supports, populated only after the first BLE connection
with the vehicle.

When building your app’s UI, use the information in this property
to determine what features you can access. The array contains all
supported features. To determine if a feature is currently supported,
call the ``status(for:)`` method.

members.name: status
members.signature: func status(for function: FunctionIdentifier) throws -> FunctionStatus?
members.comment:
Returns the current status of the specified vehicle function.

Each feature of your vehicle has one or more associated states,
which you define. For example, the door locks of a vehicle might
be in the locked or unlocked state. This method returns the state
if it is known.

- Parameters:
  - function: The function identifier for the vehicle feature you
  want to check. If you specify an unknown feature, this method throws
  an error. For a list of the vehicle’s supported features, see
  the ``supportedFunctions`` property.
- Returns: The status of the feature, or `nil` if the status is
currently unknown.
